I was waitlisted on March 30th, told all decisions would be final by April 24th, and then received an email offering me admission into the part-time and non-funded 3-year program (rather than the full-time, funded 2-year program I had applied for) on April 29th. I was told within the next week I would get my official offer of admission, and I had that same one week to accept it and pay the $250 admission fee. I emailed back 6 days later saying I had discussed with my support network and had decided to reject the offer due to national instability and uncertainty of gov financial aid, but would like to reapply in the future. I asked how to indicate this acceptance on a potential future application, as I had never received an official admission offer. Two weeks after that, I got my official admission offer and a host of emails telling me what my next steps were. All of them had inconsistent and contradictory information, including dates that were different email to email and deadlines that had passed weeks ago. One email had three different dates for the same (important) deadline. I finally got a response to the email I had sent directly to the Admissions Office, saying they were sorry to hear I was declining and informing me of the steps I needed to take to officially decline. They did not answer the other questions I had included in my email to them. Throughout all of this, my name was only spelled correctly once. We will see if I do end up reapplying in future years.

comments: Early Nov 2025 contacted potential supervisor and was encouraged to apply, end of Nov 2025 submitted application, mid Jan 2026 submitted application for L4E fellowship. Early Feb 2026 I get a Whatsapp message from my proposed secondary supervisor on a Sunday afternoon (Montreal time) asking if I'm available in the next couple of hours to discuss my application. As an international applicant in a different time zone unfortunately I was already asleep so replied first thing on Monday morning trying to arrange a time we could talk, and was told they would get back to me with a different time. The next thing I hear is on the 21st April when I get sent an email to look at the application portal where I find a generic rejection message. In the mean time I sent numerous follow up messages asking if they still wanted to talk with me but I never got a reply. McGill's website suggested that most applicants would hear back at the end of February and throughout March so towards the end of March I began to reach out by email to the proposed primary supervisor, program administrator, and L4E to see if they could give me any insight into the progress of my application or when I could expect to hear back. These emails and subsequent follow ups were also all completely ignored. I am obviously gutted about my application being rejected however given the seeming distinct lack of compassion, communication, and organisation shown by the anthropology department at McGill and the L4E it raises some major red flags to me about the quality of teaching and support that is offered by both the program and the fellowship. I would be very interested to hear from successful applicants about if this is the case? If the other applications I am still waiting on are also unsuccessful I will be applying for PhD programs again next year, however given the inadequacy of my experience this year I shan't be reapplying to McGill. Very disappointed.

I followed up with them twice in early Jan '26 (since the deadline was Jan 15), but didn't get a response. I knew it was a lost cause because I could see on LinkedIn that they were deeply, DEEPLY invested in industrial research, consulting, and other roles outside of academia. It's not a bad thing, but it certainly is worth keeping in mind. I applied anyway since I had an excellent fit with their research directions and had already sent TOEFL/GRE scores to the program. This rejection was always coming. Anyway, I have accepted another top-tier offer from elsewhere, so it doesn't matter anymore. But to anyone reading this: please do not, DO NOT apply to NUS ECE without explicit PI interest, especially if you're thinking of doing so straight out of undergrad.

comments: Canadian domestic student. Applied in early March; notified by the end of March. Also note: "The University of Western Ontario" is also known as "Western University." Additional notes: I already went to graduate school here (finished with an MSc in Industrial-Organizational Psychology in the past). I completed some additional coursework (enough to warrant a second bachelor's degree in Math) and this is what the 3.60 (standardized GPA that takes into account institution) is based on. My grade average (as calculated by the school) was an 84%, somehow (I'm not sure how they arrived at this number; I think that even including only my last two years would have resulted in an average of 83.5% so maybe they rounded?). Every course on this transcript was a math, statistics, or computer science course (only one course from computer science; everything else was a roughly even split of math or statistics). I also had three summer research internships in Math and Statistics. I did not include any GRE scores because I did not include these in my application, but if anyone's curious, my old scores (back when I got into grad school the first time) were 94th percentile analytical writing, 97th percentile verbal, and 89th percentile quantitative (and I think that's because during that year, if you got perfect, it would still only be 94th percentile because of how many people would get perfect on that section). I also had prior experience with my selected supervisor (i.e., I attended his class and worked with him for one of my summer research internships).

Dear BAH BAH BAH,
I am writing in regard to your application for admission to graduate study at the
University of Southern California. After careful review of your application and
supporting materials, the Admission Committee has asked me to inform you that we are
unable to offer you admission to the Doctor of Philosophy program in Media Arts and
Practice for Fall 2026.
We understand this must be very disappointing news. Please bear in mind that each year
the university receives applications from many more students than it can accommodate.
Admissibility is determined by the size of the applicant pool as well as student
credentials. Unfortunately, as a result we are not able to offer admission to some
students of significant ability and potential.
We encourage you to continue to work toward your educational and professional goals,
and wish you every success in your future endeavors.
Sincerely,
you.usc.edu
Timothy E. Brunold
Dean of Admission

First notification was in the portal with a two sentence rejection notice. Several days later I received an email with a more detailed explanation:  

"The Graduate Admissions Committee in the Department of English at the University of Florida has completed its review of applications and, unfortunately, has not selected you for admission.
 
This is no reflection on your academic excellence. We received more than 200 applications from talented and accomplished students all over the world for our graduate program, and we have admitted fewer than 10%. With so many excellent applicants to choose from, our decisions often came down to judgments about which students we can best support with our particular faculty expertise, our library resources, and the teaching and other training opportunities we can provide. Many of those who applied to our program can, we believe, actually be served better elsewhere. We hope that you get that opportunity, and we wish you luck and success in your future endeavors.
 
One final note: because we had so many applicants, we are unable to offer each applicant a detailed response on our Admissions Committee’s decision. Thank you for considering the University of Florida and for giving us an opportunity to review your materials. We are always amazed and humbled by the astonishing work that applicants to our program intend to do in the future. This year is no exception."

comments: Interviewed 2.10 and genuinely thought it went well. Proposed research: 19th- 20th-century American poetry; my writing sample brought existentialist thought - especially the work of Jean-Paul Sartre - into discourse with American poetics. All the indicators looks good. Then... no waitlist, no unofficial offer... I understand since before the decision came out that I had made the finalist pool but not the admit pool or waitlist (about 2 people were admitted from what I've heard; yet, if you look at the website, about 10-15 professors are seeking advisees... meaning only 2 professors, probably very distinguished, had the negotiating power to have their pick... the person I chose as a potential advisor probably didn't have the bandwidth or the care for philosophical approaches that my dissertation gestured toward...). I know now how to position myself for next cycle (I only applied to one English program this cycle, Harvard's); next time I'll be applying to all 8 Ivy English PhDs and will write dissertations that draw from the work of more senior level professors to ensure I get in.... just putting this all here because it really is a journey, and nobody was there to advise me exactly on how to go about it :)

comments: I presume it's a rejection, anyway, because surely "hmm we're struggling to figure out how to make the system display the details ... check tomorrow" is not what they'd choose for acceptances and waitlists.  I feel for the person I'm in email contact with, who sounds unsupported in their job (which perhaps also happened in 2024 if you look back in these results?).  I emailed asking when I might get my decision because it seems late.  They emailed back very promptly saying it should be in the portal.  I responded that when I log in to ApplyWeb, on the page where I can see all the universities that used ApplyWeb, there is a "decision letter" button above the "checklist" button but this doesn't appear for Cornell.  They responded that perhaps it needs to process overnight, but let them know if I still didn't see it tomorrow.  I talked to the tech support bot which suggests (Interesting to know!) that universities load a bunch of decision letters and then have to add a date and time and give permission for the student to view it (so if the college says it's there and I say it's not, they probably didn't give permission yet).  I sent that info to the kind administrative person at Cornell's History Graduate program, who thanked me for it and said it gave them an idea of a few things to go check.  Sounds like the funding cuts really hit a lot of areas -- my home department has had a lot of cuts and it's our admin person who is bearing the brunt of a lot of it.  Anyway.  Still can't see a decision in the portal, but it's apparent my application is just an administrative loose end, and this cycle has taught me that my research niche is "weird" and difficult for programs to find space for.  1a/7r/3p is I think the current tally, one pending is a Public Policy program.

I reached out to UConn because I had not heard. Only then did I get a rejection email, which essentially told me that even though I was not being considered, I wouldn't receive a rejection until after April 15th. Idk if this is a common occurrence, but I find it to be a bit disrespectful either way, after all the time we spend on these apps. The email I was sent is below:

"Thank you for your email and continued interest in UConn’s MA program. At this time, we have issued offers of acceptance to a very small number of applicants, as well as notifications to a few others that they have been placed on a selective waitlist. It is unlikely that we will move beyond our waitlist this year. Official decisions for all remaining applicants will likely be released after the April 15th deadline, as UConn adheres to the Council of Graduate Schools’ (CGS) “April 15 Resolution”: April 15 Resolution - CGS (cgsnet.org). Applicants who have received offers have until April 15th to respond."

Dear Applicant,
Thank you for the time, effort, and passion you put into your application to the UCSC Physics graduate program. There is a person behind every application, statement of purpose, and letter of recommendation, and we truly appreciate the effort you contributed applying to our program. That is what makes it challenging to inform you we are unable to recommend you for admission for this coming fall.

This was a difficult decision for our committee for two reasons: 1) this year’s applicant pool was exceptionally talented, and the level of research experience and academic dedication we saw was genuinely humbling; and 2) due to department funding and faculty research capacity we are simply unable to recommend offers of admission to all researchers we believe would thrive here.

This decision is a reflection of our departmental constraints, not a reflection of your potential as a physicist. There are many paths towards scientific inquiry, and we hope you continue pursuing your interests in physics research.

Understandably, many applicants ask us for feedback on their applications to see how they can improve in the future. Please understand due to the sheer number of requests we receive the committee is unable to provide comment on any individual's application. We trust that your continued efforts and dedication will open doors for you as you pursue your career.

Thank you again for considering UC Santa Cruz. We wish you the very best in your next chapter.
